I RESUMED A DIED ITERATION AGAIN -- THIRD SPRINT RUNNING (TD-059). The tree already held the ENTIRE US-508 implementation plus a 44-test suite, written by an iteration that expired before running its gate and before committing. If you wake to a dirty tree with agent-1 claiming a story, that is a RESUMABLE iteration, not a mess to clear: read the diff, RUN THE TARGETED TESTS, let the suite tell you the real state. It was green on arrival.
AND HERE IS THE LESSON THAT MATTERS MOST, because green is exactly where I nearly stopped: A GREEN SUITE ON INHERITED WORK PROVES THE TESTS THAT EXIST PASS -- IT DOES NOT PROVE THE RIGHT TESTS EXIST. 44 passing tests is a very convincing thing to close on. I walked the ACCEPTANCE LIST instead of the test list and found TWO real gaps, and those gaps are this iteration's actual contribution. When you resume someone else's work the hole is never in what they tested -- it is in what they never reached.
GAP 1, AND IT IS THE HONEST-INSTRUMENT ONE: ALTITUDE HAD ZERO ASSERTIONS ANYWHERE IN tests/ui. The code renders it correctly (naTile -> typed-NA) and its own comment even NAMES the hazard -- 'a zeroed altitude renders as sea level, a confident lie' -- but nothing enforced it. THE HARDEST FIELD TO PIN IS THE ONE THAT IS ALWAYS ABSENT: it has no producer on this Pi, so its only correct rendering is a gap, and a gap looks like an OVERSIGHT to the next person, who fixes it with a 0. Assert NO DIGIT AT ALL rather than == 'NA' -- the digit-free form also catches the helpful '0 ft' / '0 m' / '--- ft' variants of the same mistake. And PIN THAT THE ABSENCE STILL GETS PAINTED: an unconditionally-NA tile is precisely what a renderer cleanup deletes, and Atlas kept the field for zero-rework later, so losing the DOM slot means re-laying-out rather than re-wiring when a BMP280 lands. Five pins total.
GAP 2: A DEFAULT NO TEST EVER USES IS NOT TESTED. DEFAULT_STATE_HZ went 4 -> 10 (the whole AC-5 transport ruling), but EVERY rate test in test_imu_state_bridge.py passes stateHz=4 EXPLICITLY -- so the default path was never exercised and a silent revert would leave the suite green while the tape and g-trail visibly stutter on the panel. That is a defect only a human in a moving car ever reports. When a story changes a DEFAULT, ask which test exercises the default PATH, not the constant. Added a behavioural test plus a CROSS-ARTIFACT pin reading the shipped carousel.js IMU_POLL_MS, because A GROUNDING CLAIM IN A COMMENT IS NOT A CHECK -- the docstring asserted that grounding and nothing verified it. Writing slower than the reader polls does not slow the poll; it makes the reader re-read an unchanged file and animate nothing. Same two-correct-halves-stopped-agreeing shape as US-494/499.
TDD ON PRE-EXISTING CODE = MUTATION PROOF, and this is the reusable technique: all 5 pins passed on first run, which proves NOTHING. So I broke each defect they forbid (fabricate a sea-level altitude / drop the field / compute-but-never-paint it / revert the cadence to 4) and confirmed each went RED naming the right test. CRITICAL SAFETY DETAIL: the files held UNCOMMITTED work, so restore lives in a `finally` and I verified it by diff-stat before staging. NEVER `git checkout` to undo a mutation on a dirty file -- that is how a recovery destroys the thing it recovered.
US-507'S FLAGGED VALIDATION GAP IS NOW CLOSED BY THIS STORY: absorbing Motion into the home slot is what reaches the CIO-locked 4 cards, so the criterion I routed to the PM inbox is discharged by US-507+US-508 jointly. FIRST, READ HOW THIS ITERATION STARTED, because it is the most reusable thing here: I DID NOT START FROM A CLEAN TREE. The previous iteration had ALREADY claimed US-507 (status active in ralph_agents.json) and written the ENTIRE implementation + a 535-line test file -- then died BEFORE running the tests and BEFORE committing. `git status` showed 9 modified/untracked files I had not touched. That is TD-059 exactly (the backgrounded-gate stall) and it has now cost the first story of multiple sprints. THE RECOVERY MOVE: do NOT re-implement, and do NOT trust the work either. Read the diff, RUN THE TARGETED TESTS, and let the suite tell you what state the work is really in. Mine was one failing test away from done. If you wake up to a dirty tree with your own agent-id claiming a story, that is a resumable iteration, not a mess to clear.
AND THE FAILURE WAS A TEST-HYGIENE BUG, NOT A CODE BUG -- SECOND OCCURRENCE OF A LESSON THIS PROJECT ALREADY WROTE DOWN. My own pin asserted `"renderLtftTrendCard" not in js` to prove no dangling call survived the rename. It went RED against CORRECT code, because the COMMENT marking the deleted branch NAMES the function it replaced. Session 11 learned this identical shape on `NoInputNoOutput`/`PYEOF`. It RECURS because the two impulses pull opposite ways: good practice says document the rename, and the pin says forbid the old name. Strip comments, then grep. Expect it a third time.
AND TEST THE STRIPPER -- OVER-STRIPPING IS THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION FOR AN ABSENCE ASSERTION, because it deletes the very text the test hunts for and the pin passes VACUOUSLY (falsely green, the one failure mode a guard must not have). Concrete hazard I found before trusting it: carousel.js:2331 is `"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"` -- a STRING containing `//` that a naive line-comment strip truncates. So `_stripJsComments` is string-aware (quotes + escapes + both comment forms) and is ITSELF pinned by two tests: code landmarks survive, the SVG namespace survives, real prose goes.
THE BIGGEST DESIGN LESSON, and it is what the merge could most plausibly have broken: MERGING CARDS MUST NOT MERGE THEIR FAILURES. The obvious implementation routes the merged card through the EXISTING card-level availability check -- and then one dead UPS blanks the two LIVE instruments beside it. That is a fabricated "nothing is readable" manufactured out of one real fault, and it looks like tidy code reuse. Availability resolves PER SECTION. Pinned by test, and it is the thing to watch on the Pi.
A GATE'S VOCABULARY IS A FUNCTION OF ITS CONTAINER. As a CARD, fuel trim said "does not apply right now" by being `hidden`. As a SECTION of an always-visible card it cannot vanish without leaving a hole, so the same fact must be said in WORDS ("no engine data"). The disposition vocabulary therefore grew from TWO to THREE -- gated / no-data / live -- and collapsing gated into no-data would tell an operator with a RUNNING engine that there is no engine. Whenever a surface changes container, re-derive how it says "not applicable".
AND THE GATE IS CHECKED BEFORE THE DATA, which is the honest-instrument half: a gated section carries NO view at all, so a stale ltft-trend file left on disk from the last drive cannot paint a confident trim for an engine that is not running. Ships `data-gated="true"` so the pre-first-poll window (when "is a car connected?" is genuinely unknown) fails CLOSED.
A MERGE CAN MAKE AN OLD ASSERTION VACUOUS WITHOUT TURNING IT RED, which is the most dangerous test outcome there is. test_render_regression asserted `"LTFT Trend" not in cards` to guard the bench gate; once NO card carries that name it is true for the WRONG reason and would keep passing if the gate broke ENTIRELY. Replaced with a POSITIVE assertion that the section painted `data-gated="true"`. RULE: when a story removes the noun an absence assertion names, that assertion is DEAD -- re-aim it, do not admire the green.
DELETED the dead `ltft-trend` tick branch rather than leaving it unreachable: it still named the pre-rename `renderLtftTrendCard`, so nothing executed it and nothing proved it still RESOLVED. Same family as US-500 -- the dangerous line is the one that never runs.

SPRINT 68 (V0.29.23, F-124 Pi UI round 2) OPENED -- US-506 (the carousel nav model) DONE, 1/6. Commit f22b410. Sprint.json WAS correctly dispatched this time (6 stories, sprint-ready) -- no repeat of last session's empty-queue scramble. NEXT STORY IS US-507 (consolidate 6 cards -> 4 'Health' card), and it touches the SAME two files I just rewrote (carousel.js + dashboard.html), so re-read them from disk rather than trusting this note's description of them.\nTHE HEADLINE LESSON, and it is the one I would want back if I lost everything else: ADDING VELOCITY TO A GESTURE IS ADDING A DIMENSION, NOT REPLACING DISTANCE. The obvious refactor is to swap the 40px distance test for the 0.6 px/ms velocity test. Do that and a 5px twitch over 2ms measures 2.5 px/ms -- FOUR TIMES the flick threshold -- so the carousel pages on a stray touch and on every palm brush. Distance answers 'was this a swipe AT ALL?'; velocity answers 'what KIND of swipe?'. Two questions, two thresholds, both required, both pinned by test.\nAND THE ONE THAT NEARLY SHIPPED WRONG: DIVIDING BY A MEASUREMENT IS A FABRICATION RISK, and this fabrication is FELT rather than displayed. `travel/dtMs` with dt==0 is Infinity -> classified a FLICK -> auto-rotate RESUMES under the operator's finger while they are reading. An unmeasurable duration is NOT an infinitely fast gesture. It contributes 0 and the travel test -- a real reading -- answers instead. Same guard for a 0-width card box on a transient 0x0 layout pass. This project applies honest-instrument to RENDERED values by reflex; it applies just as hard to DERIVED values that drive BEHAVIOUR, and those are harder to spot because no pixel looks wrong.\nA CONFIG SCHEMA CAN MAKE A BAD STATE UNREACHABLE, which beats guarding for it downstream. resolveCarouselConfig accepts only finite POSITIVE numbers, so `resumeIdleS: 0` falls back to the default and can NEVER reach shouldAutoResume to disable the self-unpause. The 'a pause freezes the carousel forever' failure is not defended against at the consumer -- it is inexpressible at the source. Ask of any new tunable: which values would break the invariant, and can the resolver simply refuse them?\nRELATED, SAME FAMILY: FAIL A MISCONFIGURED INTERVAL TO **OFF**, NOT TO FAST. A non-positive autoRotateS naively means 'advance when sinceMs >= 0' = every 250ms tick. A carousel spinning at the poll rate is unusable and reads as a HARDWARE fault, so the operator debugs the wrong layer. shouldAutoAdvance and rotateProgress both return false/0 on a non-positive period. Ask of any interval: what does 0 do?\nHANG A CROSS-CUTTING SIDE EFFECT ON ONE DOCUMENT-LEVEL LISTENER, NOT N CALL SITES. 'A tap on a card or opening ANY overlay pauses' could have been 6+ per-overlay pauseAutoRotate() calls -- and overlay #7 forgets, silently, forever. ONE document pointerdown handler covers every present AND future affordance; the swipe handler resumes afterwards if the gesture turns out to be a flick. This matters directly for US-509, which ADDS an overlay: it gets pause for free and must not add its own call.\nA PROGRESS BAR MUST BE REMOVED WHEN IT STOPS, NOT FROZEN PART-FILLED. Leaving the bar at 60% while paused is the exact frozen-instrument fabrication US-497 named for the g-dot -- it promises an advance that is never coming. Same rule, different geometry. Expect it again for any future timed affordance.\nWHEN A STORY OVERTURNS A CONTRACT, THE OLD TEST IS EVIDENCE, NOT AN OBSTACLE. test_nextVisibleIndex_clampsAtTheLastVisibleCard went RED BY DESIGN. I did not delete it: I read what it was REALLY guarding (never land on a hidden card -- still true and still load-bearing), kept that assertion, inverted only the clamp expectation, and renamed it. Deleting it would have dropped a live invariant along with the dead one. FLAGGED in completionNotes so the PM sees a contract change rather than a quietly-edited test.\nSMALL BUT WILL BITE: MEASURE THE TRAVEL FRACTION AGAINST THE REAL BOX. #stage is letterbox-scaled (US-482), so a hard-coded 480 misreads travel on any panel that is not 1:1 -- and the Pi outputs 1080p. The handler reads track.getBoundingClientRect().width.\nCONFIG SEAM FOR THE REST OF THIS SPRINT: pi.display.carousel.* reaches the browser as window.DISPLAY_CAROUSEL through a NEW quoted placeholder (__DISPLAY_CAROUSEL__) on the SAME serve-time seam US-483-b built for auto-dim. I deliberately did NOT widen the autoDim placeholder to carry both -- different owners, different tuning cadences, and merging them would let an auto-dim edit break navigation. The two loaders now share _loadDisplaySection. If US-508/510/511 need config in the browser, that is the pattern; add a third placeholder, do not overload mine.\nVERIFIED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: main() is the ONLY StatesHttpServer construction site, so the new config genuinely reaches the browser. Two greps. THE PM'S SPRINT 67 DISPATCH THEN LANDED IN sprint.json WHILE I WAS WORKING -- I only noticed because `git status` showed sprint.json modified when I had never touched it. Two lessons, both Â§13 shared-checkout: (a) A COMPLETE sprint.json IS NOT THE SAME FACT AS AN EMPTY QUEUE -- check progress.txt's header and your inbox before concluding there is no work; (b) RE-READ ANY SHARED FILE IMMEDIATELY BEFORE YOU WRITE IT. Had I written the sprint.json I read at session start, I would have reverted the PM's entire dispatch. `git status` before staging is what catches this.\nCAPTURE THE BYTES BEFORE YOU WRITE THE MATCHER. This is the whole story. Atlas's note described the bug accurately and I still would have shipped it half-fixed from the description alone. I sshd to the Pi and recorded a real bluetoothctl session first: the prompt is `\\x1b[0;94m[bluetoothctl]> \\x1b[0m`. The obvious fix -- swap `#` for `>` -- leaves a SECOND trap armed, because the ANSI escape ITSELF CONTAINS A `[`, so the old greedy `\\[.+\\]#` would span from the escape into the prompt even on a `#` box. One fix, two independent defects in the same regex, and only the raw bytes show the second one. PROMPT_PATTERN now forbids `[`/`]` inside the bracket body and accepts either terminator (legacy boxes keep working, US-475's DoD asked for that).\nFREE FINDING FROM THE SAME CAPTURE, and it is load-bearing for BL-025: `devices Paired` returned EMPTY. There is NO bond of any kind on this Pi right now, on any device. That converts BL-025's bond-less diagnosis from inference to measurement. Radio reads Powered:yes, so the rfkill fix is holding. Recorded in specs/architecture.md 3.4.\nTHE REAL DELIVERABLE WAS NOT EITHER BUG -- IT WAS THE HEREDOC. The driver lived in `python3 - <<'PYEOF'`. Heredoc code cannot be imported, therefore cannot be tested, therefore two defects sat in a file that LOOKED maintained (headers, invariants, a shellcheck-clean wrapper) for months. Moved it to scripts/pair_obdlink_driver.py. If you ever find a bug inside a heredoc, the fix is not the bug -- ask why nothing could have caught it, because that answer is the story. Same shape as US-514's `a fix that only exists on the live Pi is not a fix`.\nTHE HARNESS FOUND A BUG I DID NOT KNOW EXISTED, and it is the best argument for verbatim fixtures I have. bluetoothctl REDRAWS ITS PROMPT SEVERAL TIMES AT STARTUP (prompt, padding+backspaces, `Agent registered`, prompt again). So `sendline(cmd); expect(PROMPT)` matches a STALE prompt still in the buffer and `before` comes back holding terminal PADDING as if it were the command's reply -- a SILENT WRONG ANSWER, strictly worse than the hang I was sent to fix, and it would have made every `info` read parse as `no bond`. Fix is the standard idiom: wait for the command's own pty ECHO first, then the prompt. A hand-written `prompt goes here` fixture passes this happily; only the real bytes fail it.\nTHREE DECISIONS THE PM/ATLAS MAY OVERRULE, all flagged in the routed note. (1) SUCCESS NOW MEANS A DURABLE BOND: `Pairing successful` is bluez's word for the LINK, so the driver re-reads `info` after trust and FAILS unless Paired+Bonded+Trusted -- the old script printed `--- pair + trust successful ---` having checked nothing, which was a claim, not a reading. (2) IDEMPOTENT WITHOUT --force: an existing durable bond is reported and LEFT ALONE, because re-pairing needs the dongle powered (engine on) and a reflexive `remove` on a working bond strands the car in the driveway; a PARTIAL bond IS cleared, since that half-state is exactly what makes `pair` fail AlreadyExists. (3) scan on -> wait -> scan OFF -> pair, per Atlas's live-proven ordering (an active discovery competes with the handshake on one radio).\nTEST-HYGIENE TRAP WORTH COPYING: my regression pins grepped for `NoInputNoOutput` and `PYEOF` and both FAILED -- on the header comments that DOCUMENT the defect. A pin that greps the defect's NAME fires on its own documentation. Strip comments and the module docstring (ast gives you tree.body[0].lineno/end_lineno) -- and then TEST THE STRIPPER, because a stripper that returns nothing makes every pin pass vacuously.\nGREEN (synchronous, in-loop): tests/pi/obdii = 674 passed / 1 skipped (shellcheck absent), exit 0. 33 new driver tests + 5 new wiring pins, all proven RED first. ruff clean on all 3 touched .py; bash -n clean; ran the real --dry-run and read its 7 preview lines. NOTE the backlog also carries US-475 for the same defect -- confirm with the PM which one you are closing so it is not built twice.\nTHE LESSON FROM THE FIX ITSELF, and it is the biggest one this project has learned in a month: THE DIAGNOSTIC ORDER IS RADIO -> BOND -> BIND -> CONNECT. THE HEADLINE LESSON: TO CATCH A COMPOSITION BUG, SPLIT THE HARNESS ALONG THE SEAM THE BUG CROSSED. All three defects this sprint fixed had one shape -- every part tested green and the composition was broken (S1: a dependency the entry point never injected, computeBootState was always right; S2: correct JS defeated by a stylesheet the JS cannot see; S5: three valid CSS declarations interacting to a black screen). So the backstop is TWO PROCESSES THAT CANNOT SEE EACH OTHER'S VERDICT: node runs the SHIPPED carousel.js / boot-state-poll.js against a mini-DOM and dumps the attributes (it knows nothing about CSS); Python resolves the SHIPPED stylesheet over that DOM and answers the only question that matters -- does this element have a box. Neither half can launder the other's answer. That property is what every existing UI test lacked.
THE LOAD-BEARING DETAIL, and it generalises to any DOM harness: IDL properties must REFLECT to CONTENT ATTRIBUTES. `el.hidden = true` has to land as the `hidden` ATTRIBUTE, because the attribute is what the cascade selects on. A harness storing it as a private flag would have reproduced US-495's BLIND SPOT and passed the broken stylesheet without a murmur. Everything else in mini_dom.js is scoped to the ~15 DOM methods the kits actually touch -- enumerated from the source with grep, not guessed. It is not a jsdom clone and must not grow into one.
PROVEN RED AGAINST REAL HISTORY, not asserted: `git show <fixcommit>^:<path>` gives you the actual defective artifact, and a stdlib-only module can be loaded LIVE via importlib and run. The pre-US-495 stylesheet reproduces all six overlays painting at idle; the pre-US-494 emitter, wired the way its own entry point wired it (no obdProbeFn -- that OMISSION is the bug), pins the splash with the literal 'eclipse-obd: not ready (starting)'. Because history is not guaranteed (shallow clone / CI), TWO MUTATION proofs run unconditionally beside them (delete the [hidden] guard rule; strip just its !important). Pattern worth reusing: git artifact = the literal claim, mutation = the one that still runs everywhere.

Also: restore a patched `time.monotonic` in a finally -- it is global, and the same process shells out to node moments later, under subprocess's own timeout bookkeeping.

THE HEADLINE LESSON: REVERSING AN ANIMATION IS TWO REVERSALS, AND SHIPPING ONE OF THEM IS A BLACK SCREEN. The kit flipped `animation-direction: reverse` on every class with a comment saying 'the keyframes are symmetric enough that reverse just works'. Direction was the easy half; the running ORDER also has to reverse. The boot timeline ENDS with a fadeout DELAYED 6s, and `animation-fill-mode: both` holds the reversed animation's FIRST RELEVANT keyframe through that delay -- which for direction:reverse is `to`, i.e. opacity 0. So the fill-mode that exists to prevent a flash of unstyled content pinned the mark invisible for 6 seconds of a 7-SECOND GRACE WINDOW (pi.powerWatch.smoothingSec): black for essentially the whole shutdown. Fix = reversed delay is T - (bootDelay + bootDuration), T = 6.5s; derived from splash.svg, no invented numbers, and the test RE-DERIVES them so re-timing the boot re-aims the closeout.
NOTE THE SHAPE OF THE BUG, because it will recur: three individually-correct declarations (a delay, a fill-mode, a direction) interacting. Every part had a passing test. Every surrounding component worked -- sequencer emitted, emitter wrote, .path watched the right file, server served the right page with the token, JS revealed the stage on time. The surface it revealed was black. When a UI 'does nothing' and all the parts test green, stop testing parts and start SAMPLING THE OUTPUT ON A CLOCK.
SO THAT IS WHAT THE TEST DOES: tests/ui/test_shutdown_splash_render.py resolves the shipped CSS (cascade + !important, comma-list shorthands, fill-mode/direction/delay) and samples the mark's opacity every 250ms across the real grace window read from config. RED naming every blank instant t=[1.0..6.0]. One assertion I wrote OVER-CLAIMED -- 'brightness never rises' failed on the DESIGNED throb, whose recovery genuinely raises brightness -- and I corrected the test to the honest envelope claim (max->low endpoints, second half never brighter than the first) rather than keeping a green-looking lie. Fidelity limit is stated in the file: easings treated as linear, so endpoints and the SIGN of a change are exact, mid-segment values are not; every assertion is zero-vs-nonzero or an endpoint.
A KEEP-LIST IS A COST, NOT A SAFETY NET -- the deploy half, and it generalises. US-495 keep-listed the closeout surface as 'the kit's install.sh owns those'. But a keep-listed asset is never installed, never pruned and never byte-verified; its only refresh path was the A-9 kiosk step, which is ALLOWED TO WARN AND SKIP (install.sh aborts if it cannot detect session type or chromium). So the stale hole US-495 closed for boot was still open for shutdown -- where it only shows itself DURING a shutdown, nobody watching, no re-run. Moved the whole surface into the manifest (both installers copy identical bytes from the same synced kit, so ownership costs nothing and buys the verify). Keep-list is now version.txt alone, which earns it: the deploy GENERATES it, so the manifest cannot name it. Ask of any keep-list entry: who verifies this, and are they allowed to skip?
